summary: Serverless-first design: React Native (Expo), Node.js + NestJS, TimescaleDB (PostgreSQL time-series) database on AWS Lambda + API Gateway. It keeps data in Indian regions, matches the team's languages and is estimated at $460-$890 per month.

architecture.name: serverless
architecture.justification: Node.js + NestJS runs on managed, scale-to-zero functions, so there are no servers to size or patch and idle time costs little.

alternatives.why_not: Adds service boundaries, network calls and per-service deployment that this team does not need at this scale (team 4).
Steadier cost at sustained high load, but needs a host to size, patch and monitor.

frontend.justification: React Native (Expo) matches the team's javascript skills; covers web and android from one codebase; scales on clients, JS bridge limits heavy UIs.

alternatives.why_not: Flutter scores 0.8 points lower overall, mainly on team skill fit (1.4 points) and cost (0.6 points).

tradeoffs: Native modules outside the Expo SDK need a custom development build

backend.justification: Node.js + NestJS builds on the team's existing language skills; handles many concurrent realtime connections well; modular design, microservice transports, WebSocket gateways.

alternatives.why_not: Python + Django scores 0.37 points higher, which is inside the near-tie range, and loses the tie-break: lower cost first, then complexity and operations load.

Python + FastAPI scores 0.1 points lower overall, mainly on cost (0.6 points) and compatibility with the rest of the stack (0.6 points). Estimated infrastructure about $470-$930/month versus about $370-$750/month.

tradeoffs: More boilerplate

database.justification: TimescaleDB can be placed in Mumbai (ap-south-1) to keep data in India; has headroom for the expected load; hypertables, compression and continuous aggregates; is a proven choice for iot projects. It runs as Tiger Cloud (managed TimescaleDB), the managed service from the database vendor, so backups, patching and failover are the provider's job.

alternatives.why_not: ClickHouse scores 2.7 points lower overall, mainly on data-model fit (3.0 points) and time to market (0.7 points).
MongoDB (Atlas or self-hosted) scores 4.2 points lower overall, mainly on data-model fit (4.4 points) and cost (0.6 points).

tradeoffs: Smaller managed footprint than plain Postgres

hosting.justification: AWS Lambda + API Gateway runs on AWS as preferred; can be placed in Mumbai (ap-south-1) to keep data in India; offers a 99.95% SLA, in line with the 99.9% target; automatic scale to thousands of concurrent.

alternatives.why_not: AWS EC2 (self-managed VMs) scores 0.47 points higher, which is inside the near-tie range, and loses the tie-break: lower cost first, then complexity and operations load.
AWS Elastic Beanstalk scores 0.37 points higher, which is inside the near-tie range, and loses the tie-break: lower cost first, then complexity and operations load.

tradeoffs: No long-lived connections without API Gateway websockets

High vendor lock-in: AWS Lambda + API Gateway is hard to leave once the data model and SDKs are in use.

assumptions: Load estimate: peak about 60 requests/second and about 39M requests/month from 8K users in 12 months.
Usage-priced items are shown as a band (0.75x to 1.3x of the estimate) because load figures are order-of-magnitude.
Public list prices of each product, in USD, without taxes, committed-use discounts or developer time.
The 99.9% availability target doubles or adds redundancy for hosting and database where needed.

warnings.message: SMS to Indian numbers needs DLT registration (entity, sender ID and message templates) with a telecom operator before launch; allow one to two weeks.
DPDP Act: record consent, support erasure and correction, notify breaches, and take extra care with children's data. Cross-border transfer is allowed except to countries the government restricts.

CERT-In directions (April 2022) apply to services used in India: enable logs on all systems, keep them for 180 days within India, sync clocks to an NTP source and report cyber incidents within 6 hours. Size log retention and storage for this.

Expected cost ($460-$890) is inside the $800 budget at typical load but can pass it at peak usage; watch database (TimescaleDB (PostgreSQL time-series), $180-$390) and hosting (AWS Lambda + API Gateway, $150-$240) first.

assumptions: No extra inputs supplied; neutral defaults are used (learning appetite medium, lock-in tolerance medium, budget strictness firm, no hiring plan, no mobile preference).
No cache layer: about 60 requests/second and 8,000 users in 12 months are served directly by the database or BaaS.

pipeline: filter each layer by hard constraints

robustness.summary: The same stack wins in 10 of 14 checks. It switches to Python + Django (backend), AWS Elastic Beanstalk (hosting) when time to market counted twice as much; and to AWS EC2 (self-managed VMs) (hosting) when performance counted twice as much; and to Python + Django (backend) when performance counted half as much, security counted twice as much. The runner-up scores 0.47 points higher but costs more, and stacks within 0.75 points count as a tie that the cheaper one wins.

checks.change: time to market counted twice as much
time to market counted half as much
